question: Who is legally responsible for making sure a vehicle is not overloaded?
options: The person who loaded the vehicle
The driver
The owner of the goods
The vehicle insurer
explanation: Vehicle towing and loading. You MUST NOT tow more than your licence permits, you MUST NOT overload your vehicle or trailer, and you MUST secure your load and it MUST NOT stick out dangerously. (Highway Code rule 98.)

question: When towing, what must you ensure about your load?
options: It is no wider than the towing mirrors
It is heavier at the rear than at the front
It is secure and does not stick out dangerously
It is covered with a dark sheet
explanation: Vehicle towing and loading. You MUST NOT tow more than your licence permits, you MUST NOT overload your vehicle or trailer, and you MUST secure your load and it MUST NOT stick out dangerously. (Highway Code rule 98.)

question: You are carrying a heavy load on a roof rack. What effect is this most likely to have?
options: Better fuel economy
Lighter steering at high speed
Reduced stability, especially when cornering or in side winds
Improved braking
explanation: Reduced stability, especially when cornering or in side winds. (Highway Code rule 98 / Annex 6.)

question: A trailer begins to snake from side to side while you are towing it. What should you do?
options: Ease off the accelerator and reduce speed gradually
Brake firmly and hold the steering wheel tightly
Accelerate to pull it straight
Steer sharply in the opposite direction
explanation: Ease off the accelerator and reduce speed gradually. (Highway Code rule 98 / Annex 6.)

question: When loading a trailer, where should the heaviest items be placed?
options: As high as possible to lower the centre of gravity
Low down and over the axle
At the very front
At the very back
explanation: Low down and over the axle. (Highway Code rule 98 / Annex 6.)

question: You are towing a caravan on a motorway. Which lane MUST you NOT use on a three-lane carriageway?
options: The left-hand lane
The right-hand lane
Any lane during congestion
The middle lane
explanation: The right-hand lane. (Highway Code rule 98 / Annex 6.)

question: When may a load project dangerously beyond the sides of your vehicle?
options: Never — it MUST NOT stick out dangerously
When marked with a red flag
During daylight hours only
When travelling under 30 mph
explanation: Never — it MUST NOT stick out dangerously. (Highway Code rule 98 / Annex 6.)
